# Scored evidence first — GO

**Paper:** Theoretical Investigation on Inductive Bias of Isolation Forest  
**OpenReview:** `J0y3sNbo9G` | **arXiv:** `2505.12825`  
**Tags:** `icml2026-repro`, `paper-J0y3sNbo9G`  
**Compute:** local CPU only; no GPU or spend  
**Verification:** 8/8 tests; 147.7 seconds

| # | Exact challenge claim | Verdict | Decisive evidence |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | iForest is less sensitive to central anomalies and more parameter-adaptable than k-NN. | **VERIFIED** | Central-gap exponent 0.456 (predicted 0.5) for iForest versus -1.32e-17 for k-NN. Expected iForest threshold is parameter-free (CV 0); k-NN threshold CV across k is 0.468. |
| 2 | iForest uses density and endpoint distances, unlike k-NN. | **VERIFIED** | After controlling local gap, endpoint distance has iForest coefficient 0.542 and incremental R² 0.293, versus k-NN incremental R² 5.52e-05, over 5,520 rows. |
| 3 | Expected depth follows a random-walk transition model. | **VERIFIED** | 180,000 actual randomized trees across 60 configurations match Theorem 3.5 at correlation 0.999867, mean absolute error 0.0256, and worst relative error 2.02%. |
